title: अंश ३ · अध्याय १२

items.text: (गृहस्थाचारकथनम्)
items.tr: (gṛhasthācārakathanam)

items.speaker: और्व उवाच
items.text:
देवगोब्राहमणान् सिद्धान् वृद्धाचार्यांस्तथार्चयेत् ।
द्विकालञ्च नमेत् सन्ध्यामग्नीनुपचरेत् तथा ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
devagobrāhamaṇān siddhān vṛddhācāryāṃstathārcayet |
dvikālañca namet sandhyāmagnīnupacaret tathā || 1 ||

items.text:
सदानुपहते वस्त्रे प्रशस्ताश्च महौषधीः ।
गारुडानि च रत्नानि बिभृयात् प्रयतो नरः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
sadānupahate vastre praśastāśca mahauṣadhīḥ |
gāruḍāni ca ratnāni bibhṛyāt prayato naraḥ || 2 ||

items.text:
प्रस्निग्धामलकेशश्च सुगन्धिश्चारुवेषधृक् ।
सिताः सुमनसो हृद्या बिभृयाच्च नरः सदा ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
prasnigdhāmalakeśaśca sugandhiścāruveṣadhṛk |
sitāḥ sumanaso hṛdyā bibhṛyācca naraḥ sadā || 3 ||

items.text:
किञ्चित् परस्वं न हरेन्नाल्पमप्यप्रियं वदेत् ।
प्रियञ्च नानृतं ब्रूयान्नान्यदोषानुदीरयेत् ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
kiñcit parasvaṃ na harennālpamapyapriyaṃ vadet |
priyañca nānṛtaṃ brūyānnānyadoṣānudīrayet || 4 ||

items.text:
नान्यश्रियं तथा वैरं रोचयेत् पुरुषर्षभ ।
न दुष्टं यानमारोहेत् कूलच्छाया न संश्रयेत् ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
nānyaśriyaṃ tathā vairaṃ rocayet puruṣarṣabha |
na duṣṭaṃ yānamārohet kūlacchāyā na saṃśrayet || 5 ||

items.text:
विद्विष्टपतितोन्मत्तबहुवैरादिकीटकैः ।
बन्धकी बन्धकीभर्तुः क्षुद्रानृतकथैस्सह ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
vidviṣṭapatitonmattabahuvairādikīṭakaiḥ |
bandhakī bandhakībhartuḥ kṣudrānṛtakathaissaha || 6 ||

items.text:
तथातिव्ययशीलैश्च परिवादरतैश्शठैः ।
बुधो मैत्रीं न कुर्वीत नैकः पन्थानमाश्रयेत् ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
tathātivyayaśīlaiśca parivādarataiśśaṭhaiḥ |
budho maitrīṃ na kurvīta naikaḥ panthānamāśrayet || 7 ||

items.text:
नावगाहेज्जलौघस्य वेगमग्रे नरेश्वर ।
प्रदीप्तं वेश्म न विशेन्नारोहेच्छिखरं तरोः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
nāvagāhejjalaughasya vegamagre nareśvara |
pradīptaṃ veśma na viśennārohecchikharaṃ taroḥ || 8 ||

items.text:
न कुर्याद्दन्तसङ्घर्षं कुष्णीयाच्च न नासिकाम् ।
नासंवृतमुखो जृम्भेच्छ्वासकासौ विसर्जयेत् ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
na kuryāddantasaṅgharṣaṃ kuṣṇīyācca na nāsikām |
nāsaṃvṛtamukho jṛmbhecchvāsakāsau visarjayet || 9 ||

items.text:
नोच्चैर्हसेत् सशब्दं च न मुञ्चेत् पवनं बुधः ।
नखान्न खादयेच्छिन्द्यान्न तृणं न महीं लिखेत् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
noccairhaset saśabdaṃ ca na muñcet pavanaṃ budhaḥ |
nakhānna khādayecchindyānna tṛṇaṃ na mahīṃ likhet || 10 ||

items.text:
न श्मश्रु भक्षयेल्लोष्टं न मृद्नीयाद्विचक्षणः ।
ज्योतींष्यमेध्यशस्तानि नाभिवीक्षेत च प्रभो ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
na śmaśru bhakṣayelloṣṭaṃ na mṛdnīyādvicakṣaṇaḥ |
jyotīṃṣyamedhyaśastāni nābhivīkṣeta ca prabho || 11 ||

items.text:
नग्नां परस्त्रियं चैव सूर्यं चास्तमयोदये ।
न हुङ्कुर्याच्छवं गन्धं शवगन्धो हि सोमजः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
nagnāṃ parastriyaṃ caiva sūryaṃ cāstamayodaye |
na huṅkuryācchavaṃ gandhaṃ śavagandho hi somajaḥ || 12 ||

items.text:
चतुष्पथं चैत्यतरुं श्मशानोपवनानि च ।
दुष्टस्त्रीसन्निकर्षं च वर्जयेन्निशि सर्वदा ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
catuṣpathaṃ caityataruṃ śmaśānopavanāni ca |
duṣṭastrīsannikarṣaṃ ca varjayenniśi sarvadā || 13 ||

items.text:
पूज्यदेवद्विजज्योतिश्छायां नातिक्रमेद्बुधः ।
नैकश्शून्याटवीं गच्छेत् तथा शून्यगृहे वसेत् ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
pūjyadevadvijajyotiśchāyāṃ nātikramedbudhaḥ |
naikaśśūnyāṭavīṃ gacchet tathā śūnyagṛhe vaset || 14 ||

items.text:
केशास्थिकण्टकामेध्यबलिभस्मतुषांस्तथा ।
स्नानार्द्रधरणीं चैव दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
keśāsthikaṇṭakāmedhyabalibhasmatuṣāṃstathā |
snānārdradharaṇīṃ caiva dūrataḥ parivarjayet || 15 ||

items.text:
नानार्यानाश्रयेत् कांश्चिन्न जिह्मं रोचयेद्बुधः ।
उपसर्पेन्न वै व्यालं चिरं तिष्ठेन्न वोत्थितः ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
nānāryānāśrayet kāṃścinna jihmaṃ rocayedbudhaḥ |
upasarpenna vai vyālaṃ ciraṃ tiṣṭhenna votthitaḥ || 16 ||

items.text:
अतीव जागरस्वप्ने तद्वत्स्नानासने बुधः ।
न सेवेत तथा शय्यां व्यायामं च नरेश्वर ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
atīva jāgarasvapne tadvatsnānāsane budhaḥ |
na seveta tathā śayyāṃ vyāyāmaṃ ca nareśvara || 17 ||

items.text:
दंष्ट्रिणः शृङ्गिणश्चैव प्राज्ञो दूरेण वर्जयेत् ।
अवश्यायं च राजेन्द्र पुरोवातातपौ तथा ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
daṃṣṭriṇaḥ śṛṅgiṇaścaiva prājño dūreṇa varjayet |
avaśyāyaṃ ca rājendra purovātātapau tathā || 18 ||

items.text:
न स्नायान्न स्वपेन्नग्नो न चैवोपस्पृशेद्बुधः ।
मुक्तकेशश्च नाचामेद्देवाद्यर्चां च वर्जयेत् ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
na snāyānna svapennagno na caivopaspṛśedbudhaḥ |
muktakeśaśca nācāmeddevādyarcāṃ ca varjayet || 19 ||

items.text:
होमदेवार्चनाद्यासु क्रियास्वाचमने तथा ।
नैकवस्त्रः प्रवर्तेत द्विजवाचनिके जपे ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
homadevārcanādyāsu kriyāsvācamane tathā |
naikavastraḥ pravarteta dvijavācanike jape || 20 ||

items.text:
नासमञ्जसशीलैस्तु सहासीत कथञ्चन ।
सद्वृत्तसन्निकर्षो हि क्षणार्द्धमपि शस्यते ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
nāsamañjasaśīlaistu sahāsīta kathañcana |
sadvṛttasannikarṣo hi kṣaṇārddhamapi śasyate || 21 ||

items.text:
विरोधं नोत्तमैर्गच्छेन्नाधमैश्च सदा बुधः ।
विवाहश्च विवादश्च तुल्यशीलैर्नृपेष्यते ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
virodhaṃ nottamairgacchennādhamaiśca sadā budhaḥ |
vivāhaśca vivādaśca tulyaśīlairnṛpeṣyate || 22 ||

items.text:
नारभेत कलिं प्राज्ञः शुष्कवैरञ्च वर्जयेत् ।
अप्यल्पहानिः सोढव्या वैरेणार्थागमं त्यजेत् ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
nārabheta kaliṃ prājñaḥ śuṣkavairañca varjayet |
apyalpahāniḥ soḍhavyā vaireṇārthāgamaṃ tyajet || 23 ||

items.text:
स्नातो नाङ्गानि सम्मार्जेत् स्नानशाट्या न पाणिना ।
न च निर्धूनयेत् केशान् नाचामेच्चैव चोत्थितः ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
snāto nāṅgāni sammārjet snānaśāṭyā na pāṇinā |
na ca nirdhūnayet keśān nācāmeccaiva cotthitaḥ || 24 ||

items.text:
पादेन नाक्रमेत् पादं न पूज्याभिमुखं नयेत् ।
नोच्चासनं गुरोरग्रे भजेताविनयान्वितः ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
pādena nākramet pādaṃ na pūjyābhimukhaṃ nayet |
noccāsanaṃ guroragre bhajetāvinayānvitaḥ || 25 ||

items.text:
अपसव्यं न गच्छेच्च देवागारचतुष्पथान् ।
माङ्गल्यपूज्यांश्च तथा विपरीतान्न दक्षिणम् ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
apasavyaṃ na gacchecca devāgāracatuṣpathān |
māṅgalyapūjyāṃśca tathā viparītānna dakṣiṇam || 26 ||

items.text:
सोमार्काग्न्यम्बुवायूनां पूज्यानाञ्च न सम्मुखम् ।
कुर्यान्निष्ठीवविण्मूत्रसमुत्सर्गञ्च पण्डितः ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
somārkāgnyambuvāyūnāṃ pūjyānāñca na sammukham |
kuryānniṣṭhīvaviṇmūtrasamutsargañca paṇḍitaḥ || 27 ||

items.text:
तिष्ठन्न मूत्रयेत् तद्वत् पथिष्वपि न मूत्रयेत् ।
श्लैष्मविण्मूत्ररक्तानि सर्वदैव न लङ्घयेत् ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
tiṣṭhanna mūtrayet tadvat pathiṣvapi na mūtrayet |
ślaiṣmaviṇmūtraraktāni sarvadaiva na laṅghayet || 28 ||

items.text:
श्लेष्मशिङ्घाणिकोत्सर्गो नान्नकाले प्रशस्यते ।
बलिमङ्गलजप्यादौ न होमे न महाजने ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr:
śleṣmaśiṅghāṇikotsargo nānnakāle praśasyate |
balimaṅgalajapyādau na home na mahājane || 29 ||

items.text:
योषितो नावमन्येत न चासां विश्वसेद् बुधः ।
न चैवेर्ष्या र्भवेत्तासु न धिक्कुर्यात् कदाचन ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr:
yoṣito nāvamanyeta na cāsāṃ viśvased budhaḥ |
na caiverṣyā rbhavettāsu na dhikkuryāt kadācana || 30 ||

items.text:
माङ्गल्यपुष्परत्नाज्यपूज्याननभिवाद्य च ।
न निष्क्रमेद्गृहात् प्राज्ञः सदाचारपरो नरः ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr:
māṅgalyapuṣparatnājyapūjyānanabhivādya ca |
na niṣkramedgṛhāt prājñaḥ sadācāraparo naraḥ || 31 ||

items.text:
चतुष्पथान् नमस्कुर्यात् काले होमपरो भवेत् ।
दीनानभ्युद्धरेत् साधूनुपासीत बहुश्रुतान् ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr:
catuṣpathān namaskuryāt kāle homaparo bhavet |
dīnānabhyuddharet sādhūnupāsīta bahuśrutān || 32 ||

items.text:
देवर्षिपूजकः सम्यक् पितृपिण्डोदकप्रदः ।
सत्कर्ता चातिथीनां यः स लोकानुत्तमान् व्रजेत् ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr:
devarṣipūjakaḥ samyak pitṛpiṇḍodakapradaḥ |
satkartā cātithīnāṃ yaḥ sa lokānuttamān vrajet || 33 ||

items.text:
हितं मितं प्रियं काले वश्यात्मा योऽभिभाषते ।
स याति लोकानाह्लादहेतुभूतान् नृपाक्षयान् ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr:
hitaṃ mitaṃ priyaṃ kāle vaśyātmā yo'bhibhāṣate |
sa yāti lokānāhlādahetubhūtān nṛpākṣayān || 34 ||

items.text:
धीमान् ह्रीमान् क्षमायुक्तो ह्यास्तिको विनयान्वितः ।
विद्याभिजनवृद्धानां याति लोकाननुत्तमान् ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr:
dhīmān hrīmān kṣamāyukto hyāstiko vinayānvitaḥ |
vidyābhijanavṛddhānāṃ yāti lokānanuttamān || 35 ||

items.text:
अकालगर्जितादौ च पर्वस्वाशौचकादिषु ।
अनध्यायं बुधः कुर्यादुपरागादिके तथा ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr:
akālagarjitādau ca parvasvāśaucakādiṣu |
anadhyāyaṃ budhaḥ kuryāduparāgādike tathā || 36 ||

items.text:
शमं नयति यः क्रुद्धान् सर्वबन्धुरमत्सरी ।
भीताश्वासनकृत् साधुः स्वर्गस्तस्याल्पकं फलम् ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr:
śamaṃ nayati yaḥ kruddhān sarvabandhuramatsarī |
bhītāśvāsanakṛt sādhuḥ svargastasyālpakaṃ phalam || 37 ||

items.text:
वर्षातपादिषु च्छत्री दण्डी रात्र्यटवीषु च ।
शरीरत्राणकामो वै सोपानत्कः सदा व्रजेत् ॥ ३८ ॥
items.tr:
varṣātapādiṣu cchatrī daṇḍī rātryaṭavīṣu ca |
śarīratrāṇakāmo vai sopānatkaḥ sadā vrajet || 38 ||

items.text:
नोर्ध्वं न तिर्यग्दूरं वा न पश्यन् पर्यटेद्बुधः ।
युगमात्रं महीपृष्ठं नरो गच्छेद्विलोकयन् ॥ ३९ ॥
items.tr:
nordhvaṃ na tiryagdūraṃ vā na paśyan paryaṭedbudhaḥ |
yugamātraṃ mahīpṛṣṭhaṃ naro gacchedvilokayan || 39 ||

items.text:
दोषहेतूनशेषांश्च वश्यात्मा यो निरस्यति ।
तस्य धर्मार्थकामानां हानिर्नाल्पापि जायते ॥ ४० ॥
items.tr:
doṣahetūnaśeṣāṃśca vaśyātmā yo nirasyati |
tasya dharmārthakāmānāṃ hānirnālpāpi jāyate || 40 ||

items.text:
सदाचाररतः प्राज्ञो विद्याविनयशिक्षितः ।
पापेऽप्यपापः परुषे ह्यभिधत्ते प्रियाणि यः ।
मैत्रीद्रवान्तःकरणस्तस्य मुक्तिः करे स्थिता ॥ ४१ ॥
items.tr:
sadācārarataḥ prājño vidyāvinayaśikṣitaḥ |
pāpe'pyapāpaḥ paruṣe hyabhidhatte priyāṇi yaḥ |
maitrīdravāntaḥkaraṇastasya muktiḥ kare sthitā || 41 ||

items.text:
ये कामक्रोधलोभानां वीतरागा न गोचरे ।
सदाचारस्थितास्तेषामनुभावैर्धृता मही ॥ ४२ ॥
items.tr:
ye kāmakrodhalobhānāṃ vītarāgā na gocare |
sadācārasthitāsteṣāmanubhāvairdhṛtā mahī || 42 ||

items.text:
तस्मात् सत्यं वदेत् प्राज्ञो यत् परप्रीतिकारणम् ।
सत्यं यत् परदुःखाय तत्र मौनपरो भवेत् ॥ ४३ ॥
items.tr:
tasmāt satyaṃ vadet prājño yat paraprītikāraṇam |
satyaṃ yat paraduḥkhāya tatra maunaparo bhavet || 43 ||

items.text:
प्रियमुक्तं हितं नैतदिति मत्वा न तद्वदेत् ।
श्रेयस्तत्र हितं वाक्यं यद्यप्यत्यन्तमप्रियम् ॥ ४४ ॥
items.tr:
priyamuktaṃ hitaṃ naitaditi matvā na tadvadet |
śreyastatra hitaṃ vākyaṃ yadyapyatyantamapriyam || 44 ||

items.text:
प्राणिनामुपकाराय यथैवेह परत्र च ।
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा तदेव मतिमान् भजेत् ॥ ४५ ॥
items.tr:
prāṇināmupakārāya yathaiveha paratra ca |
karmaṇā manasā vācā tadeva matimān bhajet || 45 ||

en_chapter: Alurva said:—"The householder should venerate gods, king, Brāhmanas, saints, aged persons and holy preceptors. He should also observe duly the two Sandhyas and offer oblations to fire. He should use untorn garments, delicate herbs and flowers, wear emeralds and other precious stones, keep his hair neat and clean, perfume his body with delicious unguents and should always go out handsomely dressed and decorated with garlands and white flowers. He should not misappropriate another's property nor should treat him unkindly. He should always speak amiably and the truth and should not speak out publicly another's faults. O foremost of men, he should not envy another's prosperity—nor should he create enmity with another; he should not use a broken conveyance, nor should he sit under the shadow of a tree on the banks of a river. The wise should not make friends with, nor should they wend the same way with, one who is hated, who is a sinner or a drunkard, who has many enemies, or who is lousy, with a harlot or her gallant, with a pauper or a with a prodigal, a slanderer or a knave. A man should not bathe in river when it is ebb-tide, should not enter a house when it is on fire nor climb to the top of a tree; nor (when in the company of others) clean his teeth, nor blow his nose nor grape without covering his mouth, nor clean his throat, nor cough, nor laugh loudly, nor emit wind with noise, nor bite his nails, nor cut grass, nor scratch ground, nor put his beard into his mouth, nor crumble a clod of clay, nor look upon the planets when he is unclean. He should not see another's wife when she is naked nor see the sun at the time of its rising or setting. He should not express disgust at a dead body for the odour of it is the produce of the moon. He should avoid, during the night, the place where four roads meet, the village tree, the forest adjacent to a cremation ground and a loose woman. The wise should not pass across the shadow of a venerable person, of an image of a deity, of a flag and of a heavenly luminary. He should not travel alone in a forest nor sleep alone in an empty house. He should live at a distance from hair, bones, thorn, filth, remnants of offerings, ashes, chaff and earth wet with water in which another has bathed. He should not seek the shelter of a degraded wight and should renounce the company of wily persons. He should not approach voracious animals and should not lie down on bed long after sleep is broken. He should not, for a too long time, lie down on bed, sleep, keep up nights, sit and take exercise. The wise should avoid, even at a distance, animals with tusks and horns and exposure to frost, wind and sunshine. A man should neither bathe, nor sleep nor rinse his mouth when he is naked; he should not wash his mouth nor perform any sacred rite with his waistband loosened. Nor he should, with one piece of cloth on, offer oblations to fire, sacrifice to the celestials, wash his mouth, salute a Brāhman or utter a prayer. He should not associate with evil companions—the intercourse for half an instant, the pious is desirable. The wise should not quarrel men inferior or superior to them; dispute and marriage with equals are always desirable. The wise should never enter into dispute and should always avoid useless enmity. It is better to suffer a trifling loss but he should not acquire wealth by hostility.

"When bathed he should not wipe his limbs with the cloth he has put on nor with his hands; he should not shake his hair nor rinse his mouth before he has risen. He should not put one foot upon another nor spread out his foot before his elders but should modestly sit in a posture called Verāsana i.e., on his knees. He should not go round a temple upon his left hand nor circumambulate any venerable object in the reverse direction. The wise should not spit nor void impurities before the moon, fire, the sun, water, wind, or any respectable person. Nor should he pass urine standing or upon a public way; he should not pass over phlegm, ordure, urine or blood; nor should he spit forth the mucus of the throat at the time of eating, offering sacrifices or oblations or reciting prayers or before a respectable person.

"A man should not treat women disrespectfully nor should he place too much confidence in them. He should not deal with them impatiently nor should he give them supremacy in important matters. O king, wise persons, ever treading the path of morality, should not issue out of his house without saluting the chaplets, flowers, jewels, clarified butter and venerable persons. He should salute the places where four roads meet, perform sacrifices at proper seasons, relieve the poor and venerate the learned and good-natured. He who worships the celestials and saints, gives cakes and water to the manes, and performs hospitality, attains to exalted stations after death. He who speaks wisely, moderately and compassionately proceeds to the regions which are the perpetual sources of bliss. He who is intelligent, bashful, forgiving, god-fearing and humble, proceeds to the region which is attainable by the learned and those born in a pious race.

"The wise should not read the Vedas on the Parva days, on impure seasons, upon untimetely thunder and the occurrence of eclipses. The attainment of heaven is a trifling thing to him who allays the anger of the angry, who is friend to all and freed from malice, and who removes the fear of the pious. A man should use an umbrella to protect him against the sun and rain; he should carry a rod when he goes by night or through a forest and he should use shoes if he wishes to save his body from being hurt. As he proceeds he should not look up nor about him, nor afar off but keep his eyes upon the ground to the extent of a couple of yards.

"He, who, having controlled himself, puts a stop to the sources of all these imperfections, meets with no obstacle in the acquisition of piety, wealth and desire. Final emancipation is in his grasp, who is sinless towards them who commit mischief by him, who speaks amicably to them who use harsh words and whose soul melts with the benevolence. The earth is upheld by the truthfulness of those who have controlled their passions, and who, always following pious observances, are not sullied by desire, covetousness and anger. A man should therefore speak truth when it is agreeable and he should be silent when that truth would give pain. He should avoid agreeable words when they are detrimental and unreasonable, for it is always better to speak those disagreeable words which would produce salutary effect, although it would give offence. A prudent man should always cultivate that, in act, thought and speech, which conduces to the well-being of all living creatures both in this world and the next".
